subject: psychology

moments.title: Remembering
moments.body: Bartlett uses the Native American folktale 'War of the Ghosts' in serial reproduction. Participants distort the story in culturally systematic ways.

moments.title: Bransford and Johnson context studies
moments.body: Comprehension and recall depend on having an appropriate schema at encoding.
moments.takeaway: Without a schema, even simple text is hard to remember.

moments.title: Brewer and Treyens office study
moments.body: Participants in a waiting room later 'recall' schema-consistent items (books) that were not present.
moments.takeaway: Schemas insert content as well as distort it.

now.title: Schema theory and eyewitness memory
now.body: Schema-driven distortions are central to modern accounts of eyewitness error and false memory.
now.open_questions: How can interview protocols minimise schema-driven distortion in legal contexts?

reflection: Bartlett's social-anthropological framing was ignored under behaviourism, then rediscovered.
